title: 2002 Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon: Rally Roots and Reliability 🔥

history.fact: In 2001, Subaru introduced the WRX to America, bringing rally performance to the masses.

scenes.headline: Value Performance
scenes.narration: A turbocharged car giving you 227 horsepower for about $19,500 today. That’s the 2002 Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon. Designed for thrill-seekers who need space.

scenes.headline: Rally Origins
scenes.narration: Subaru unleashed rally tech to the public with this model. Its debut in 2001 marked a pivotal moment for enthusiasts in the U.S. Affordable adrenaline, thanks to its rally roots.

scenes.headline: Power & Torque
scenes.narration: Under the hood, it packs a 2.0L turbocharged flat-4. Delivering 227 horsepower and 217 lb-ft of torque to all four wheels. The five-speed manual gives drivers complete control.

scenes.headline: AWD System
scenes.narration: The WRX employs a sophisticated all-wheel-drive system. Enhancing grip on any terrain, be it snow or gravel. It became synonymous with Subaru's reputation for reliability.

scenes.headline: MOMO Steering
scenes.narration: Inside, a leather-wrapped MOMO steering wheel hints at its sporty pedigree. Paired with a boost gauge, it keeps the driver engaged. Comfort and control in every twist and turn.

scenes.headline: Functional Design
scenes.narration: A functional hood scoop ensures optimal engine cooling. Its muscular design signals intent on the road.

scenes.headline: Final Question
scenes.narration: Would you choose rally-proven AWD and turbo power over a newer tech-centric rival? The WRX Wagon showcases performance that remains impressive.

sections.Highlights: THIS...is a 2002 Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon, finished in Platinum Silver Metallic with a blue and gray interior. This WRX is equipped with the desirable 5-speed manual transmission, and the odometer indicates approximately 49,500 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or odometer discrepancies in this Subaru's past. It also lists just one North Carolina owner from new. Factory equipment on this WRX includes a viscous limited-slip rear differential, a sport-tuned suspension system, cloth upholstery, a leather-wrapped MOMO steering wheel, a boost gauge, air conditioning, and a CD player. The selling dealer reports no modifications. The 2nd-generation Impreza made its debut for the 2001 model year, and it spawned the first WRX sold on the American market. Like the standard Impreza, the WRX was offered as a sedan and as a station wagon. The WRX (World Rally eXperimental) gained rally-bred upgrades including a more powerful engine, a firmer suspension, and a more muscular-looking design characterized by a functional hood scoop and a rear spoiler. Power comes from a 2.0-liter turbocharged flat 4 engine, rated at 227 horsepower and 217 lb-ft. Output is sent to all 4 wheels through a 5-speed manual transmission.
